title: Temperature-Linked Phantom Drain Trend
dataSources: Tesla vehicle and charge state (`tesla:vehicle`, `tesla:charge`), OBD-II PIDs (`obd:pid`), Smart EV charger sessions (`evcharger:session`).
app: Tesla Fleet API / TeslaMate, TeslaFi, and generic OBD-II / Smartcar / charger APIs via HEC scripted inputs and MQTT.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=tesla:vehicle parked="true"
| bin _time span=1d
| stats earliest(battery_pct) as start_pct, latest(battery_pct) as end_pct, avg(outside_temp_c) as avg_temp by vin _time
| eval loss_pct=start_pct-end_pct
| where loss_pct>3
| sort - loss_pct
description: Quantifies parked battery loss by day so you can see whether cold snaps, heat, or background features are driving the famous EV phantom drain problem.
value: Battery drain feels mysterious until it is grouped by weather and parked time; a simple daily loss table reveals whether the culprit is the environment or the vehicle settings.
implementation: Ingest parked-state battery percentage and ambient temperature; schedule daily and trend drain on days above your normal loss rate.
visualization: Daily chart of parked battery loss with average outside temperature.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Tesla Fleet API / TeslaMate — TeslaMate MQTT/Postgres export or Fleet API poll → HEC.
• **Subcategory context**: Connected Cars & EVs — typical feeds: Tesla vehicle/charge state (`tesla:vehicle`, `tesla:charge`), TeslaMate MQTT/Postgres, OBD-II PIDs (`obd:pid`), Smartcar API (`smartcar:vehicle`), EV charger sessions (`evcharger:session`)..
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `tesla:vehicle`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Tesla Fleet API / TeslaMate** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=tesla:vehicle`.

**Collection method:** TeslaMate MQTT/Postgres export or Fleet API poll → HEC.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `vehicle_data / charge_state endpoints`.

**Suggested poll interval:** 300s while charging, 900s otherwise.

**Key fields to extract:** `battery_level, charge_rate, charge_energy_added, latitude, longitude`.

**Typical connector stack:** Tesla Fleet API / TeslaMate, Teslafi, and generic OBD-II / Smartcar / manufacturer APIs via HEC scripted inputs and MQTT..

**Author notes:** Ingest parked-state battery percentage and ambient temperature; schedule daily and trend drain on days above your normal loss rate.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "tesla:vehicle", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=tesla:vehicle earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Temperature-Linked Phantom Drain Trend** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=tesla:vehicle`) across the full search range. It applies numeric thresholds on `loss_pct` (> 3) after earliest, latest, avg — tune these constants to your household baseline.

**Fields this search depends on:** `_time`, `loss_pct`, `vin`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=tesla:vehicle parked="true"
| bin _time span=1d
| stats earliest(battery_pct) as start_pct, latest(battery_pct) as end_pct, avg(outside_temp_c) as avg_temp by vin _time
| eval loss_pct=start_pct-end_pct
| where loss_pct>3
| sort - loss_pct
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Tesla app → Energy / Charging screen. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=tesla:vehicle earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table _time, loss_pct, vin
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=tesla:vehicle earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

**(d) Threshold calibration:** Profile `loss_pct` before alerting:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=tesla:vehicle earliest=-30d
| stats perc50(loss_pct) AS p50 perc90(loss_pct) AS p90 perc99(loss_pct) AS p99 max(loss_pct) AS hi
```

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.3.12: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Daily Chart Of Parked Battery Loss With Average Outside Temperature (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Tesla Fleet API / TeslaMate — no Tesla Fleet API / TeslaMate events / missing fields:** If `tesla:vehicle` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Tesla Fleet API / TeslaMate connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Tesla Fleet API / TeslaMate — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Tesla Fleet API / TeslaMate JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=tesla:vehicle | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Tesla Fleet API / TeslaMate — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Tesla Fleet API / TeslaMate — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Tesla Fleet API / TeslaMate APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Bucket misalignment:** `span=1d` buckets on UTC by default — if your routine is local-time based, add `| eval _time=_time + (local_offset)` or use `@d` / `@w` snap.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `1d` buckets.
